title: Baseline measurement
purpose: Record the problem as it normally occurs, so later tests have a reference.
preconditions: Sensors are placed where the problem is heard or felt
Interface gain set so the loudest moment stays below -6 dBFS
Automatic gain control and audio enhancements are OFF
confounds: Changing background noise (traffic, people)
Equipment cycling on its own (thermostat, fan curves)

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Keep the sensors fixed for the rest of the investigation. Note their positions. Keep the room as quiet as normal use allows.
steps.expert_note: Position ids anchor comparability; changing them invalidates later comparisons.

steps.title: Record baseline
steps.instruction: Recording the normal situation. Stay quiet and still.

success: Two clean baseline captures are stored.

title: Equipment on/off comparison
purpose: Test whether {target} contributes to the problem by switching it off and back on (A-B-A design).
preconditions: {target} can be switched off safely without affecting other equipment
Sensors stay in exactly the same place
confounds: Other equipment changing state at the same time
Background noise changing between conditions
Switching {target} off also stops something else (shared power strip, cooling)
safety: Only switch equipment off if it is safe and normal to do so. Do not open equipment or bypass interlocks.

steps.title: {target} ON
steps.instruction: With {target} running normally, record.

steps.title: Switch off
steps.instruction: Switch {target} OFF. Change nothing else. Wait until it has fully stopped (fans spun down).

steps.title: {target} OFF
steps.instruction: Record with {target} off.

steps.title: Switch on again
steps.instruction: Switch {target} back ON and let it reach normal operation.

steps.title: {target} ON again
steps.instruction: Record again with {target} on. This checks that nothing else changed.

success: A comparable on/off/on sequence exists for {target}.

title: Source location survey
purpose: Move the microphone between positions near candidate sources to find where the problem is loudest.
preconditions: Equipment stays in its problem state throughout
confounds: Room modes: at low frequency the loudest spot may be a room corner, not the source
Moving the mic changes its distance to every source

steps.title: Position P1
steps.instruction: Place the microphone about 30 cm from the first candidate source (P1).

steps.title: Position P2
steps.instruction: Move the microphone about 30 cm from the second candidate source (P2).

steps.title: Position P3
steps.instruction: Move the microphone to a third position (P3), for example the room centre or another candidate.

success: Levels at three positions are compared.

title: Receiver position survey
purpose: Check how the problem varies across the positions where it matters (listening position, vocal mic spot).
confounds: Standing waves give strong level changes over short distances at low frequency

steps.title: Receiver R1
steps.instruction: Place the microphone at the main receiver position (R1).

steps.title: Receiver R2
steps.instruction: Move 50 cm to the side (R2).

steps.title: Receiver R3
steps.instruction: Move 50 cm to the other side (R3).

title: Contact sensor survey
purpose: Move a contact sensor across objects (desk, stand, floor, equipment case) to find where vibration is strongest.
preconditions: Use the same mounting method (wax, tape) at every point
confounds: Contact pickups also respond to airborne sound
Mounting quality changes sensitivity

steps.title: Point C1
steps.instruction: Mount the contact sensor on the first object (C1), for example the desk top.

steps.title: Point C2
steps.instruction: Move it to the second object (C2), for example the equipment case.

steps.title: Point C3
steps.instruction: Move it to a third object (C3), for example the floor or the mic stand.

success: Relative vibration at three points is compared.

title: Accelerometer vibration survey
purpose: Measure vibration at several points with an accelerometer (physical units when calibrated).
preconditions: Accelerometer mounted rigidly (stud, magnet, or thin wax) with a consistent orientation
confounds: Mounting resonance of a soft mount
Cable whip
safety: Do not mount sensors on moving parts

steps.title: Point V1
steps.instruction: Mount the accelerometer at V1 (closest to the suspected source).

steps.title: Point V2
steps.instruction: Move to V2 (along the suspected path).

steps.title: Point V3
steps.instruction: Move to V3 (at the receiver).

success: Vibration along the path is compared.

title: Loudspeaker buzz / rattle assessment
purpose: Play a slow, quiet sine sweep through {target} and detect buzzes and rattles, with the frequencies where they occur.
preconditions: {target} connected to the selected output device
Output level starts low; raise it only as far as normal listening
confounds: Objects in the room rattling (not the speaker)
Feedback if the mic is close to the speaker at high gain
safety: The test signal is limited to -12 dBFS and stops automatically after the sweep
Keep ears away from the speaker; stop immediately if anything sounds damaged

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Place the microphone 30-50 cm in front of {target}. Set the amplifier volume low. Arm the test signal when asked.

steps.title: Sweep
steps.instruction: A slow sweep from 30 Hz to 2 kHz plays through {target}. Listen for buzzes.

success: Buzz events and their sweep frequencies are reported.

title: Resonance (tap) test
purpose: Tap {object} gently to find its natural (ringing) frequencies and compare them with the problem tones.
preconditions: The equipment that causes the problem is switched OFF during tapping, if possible
confounds: Ringing of the sensor mount itself
Tapping too hard (clipping)
safety: Tap gently with a knuckle or rubber mallet; never strike fragile or energised equipment

steps.title: Tap {object}
steps.instruction: Tap {object} gently about once every two seconds near the sensor, until recording ends.

title: Isolation comparison
purpose: Test whether vibration travelling from {target} through its supports matters, by adding isolation (pads, feet, decoupling).
preconditions: {target} keeps running in the same state throughout
Sensors stay fixed
confounds: Moving {target} while isolating it also changes its distance to the mic
Isolation pads that change the source (for example blocking cooling vents)
safety: Keep cooling vents free; lift equipment safely

steps.title: Before isolation
steps.instruction: Record with {target} as it is now.

steps.title: Add isolation
steps.instruction: Add the isolation under {target}. Do not move it relative to the microphone, and change nothing else. Describe what you did.

steps.title: After isolation
steps.instruction: Record again with the isolation in place.

success: The effect of isolation on the problem is quantified.

title: Damping comparison
purpose: Test whether {object} is ringing (resonating) by adding damping material or mass to it.
preconditions: Problem equipment keeps running in the same state
confounds: Added material that also blocks airborne sound (changes the airborne path too)

steps.title: Before damping
steps.instruction: Record the current situation.

steps.title: Add damping
steps.instruction: Add damping to {object} (for example a heavy book, damping pad or a hand pressed firmly on it). Change nothing else.

steps.title: After damping
steps.instruction: Record with the damping in place.

success: The effect of damping is quantified.

title: Mounting change comparison
purpose: Test the transmission path by moving {target} to a different support (floor stand, another table) without changing its operation.
preconditions: {target} can be moved safely while keeping the same distance to the receiver where possible
confounds: Distance to the microphone changes when equipment is moved
Cables pulling on the old support
safety: Lift equipment safely and keep cables strain-free

steps.title: Original mounting
steps.instruction: Record with {target} on its original support.

steps.title: Move to another support
steps.instruction: Move {target} to the new support. Keep its distance to the microphone the same. Describe what you did.

steps.title: New mounting
steps.instruction: Record with {target} on the new support.

success: The structural path contribution is estimated.

title: Electrical hum / recording-chain test
purpose: Find out whether a hum or buzz is in the room or is generated electrically in the recording chain.
preconditions: Phantom power OFF before unplugging condenser microphones
confounds: Unplugging changes grounding (a ground loop can disappear or appear)
Hum radiated by a nearby transformer into the cable
safety: Turn phantom power off before disconnecting a microphone; turn monitors down first to avoid pops

steps.title: Normal
steps.instruction: Record with the microphone connected as usual.

steps.title: Disconnect the microphone
steps.instruction: Turn phantom power off, then unplug the microphone at the interface. Leave the interface gain exactly the same.

steps.title: Input without microphone
steps.instruction: Record with no microphone connected.

success: Hum is classified as present or absent without the microphone.

title: Airborne-pickup control for a contact sensor
purpose: Check whether the contact sensor's signal is real structural vibration or airborne sound picked up by the sensor.
preconditions: A soft support (foam, folded cloth) to rest the sensor on next to its mounting point
confounds: Different airborne exposure if the sensor is moved far away

steps.title: Sensor mounted
steps.instruction: Record with the contact sensor firmly mounted at its point.

steps.title: Decouple the sensor
steps.instruction: Remove the sensor and rest it on foam right next to the same point, so it no longer touches the structure.

steps.title: Sensor decoupled
steps.instruction: Record with the sensor resting on foam (same place, not touching).

success: The structural share of the contact signal is known.

title: Aliasing check
purpose: Check whether a tone is real or an alias of ultrasonic content, by recording at two sample rates.
preconditions: The audio interface supports both 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz
confounds: The source changing between the two captures

steps.title: Record at 48 kHz
steps.instruction: Recording at 48 kHz.

steps.title: Record at 44.1 kHz
steps.instruction: Recording at 44.1 kHz.

success: Tones that move with sample rate are identified as aliases.

title: Fix verification
purpose: Check, with repeated measurements, whether a remedy measurably improved the problem.
preconditions: Sensors stay exactly in place
Equipment runs in the same state before and after
confounds: A remedy that changes the source and the path at the same time cannot be attributed to either
Background noise changes

steps.title: Before the fix
steps.instruction: Record the problem before applying the fix.

steps.title: Apply the fix
steps.instruction: Apply the remedy. Describe it and tick what it changes (source, transmission path, receiver, measurement setup).

steps.title: After the fix
steps.instruction: Record again with the fix in place.

success: The improvement (or lack of one) is quantified with measured repeatability.
